sources: President Donald Trump, surprise White House briefing-room appearance after meeting Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani (with VP JD Vance); Trump's Truth Social post; Qatari PM's X post
fault_line: Is the war actually over, or is 'effectively over' just a new name for a blockade that never lifts — and who pays while the status quo continues? Comment threads split between 'peace through strength, thank you Mr Presid

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- he said it] After a ~45-minute closed-door meeting with Qatar's PM (recorded at 0000-02 as ended with no readout at the time), Trump told reporters: 'Iran, militarily, is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo.' 'At this point... taking military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing, but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes.' 'We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon.' He also claimed the US had 'destroyed' Iran's military and that Iran has been 'decapitated', while seeking a long-term solution to 'defang' the nuclear programme. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the war is over] Trump framed the conflict as militarily finished. [VERIFIED FACT -- what 'status quo' means] The status quo = continuation of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports ('the greatest naval blockade in the history of our country. Probably in the history of the world') plus the newly announced Task Force Iron Gate cutting trade by land and through the Caspian Sea. Trump said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait 'and others would prefer the status quo'. On Truth Social he wrote all had agreed 'Iran cannot have a Nuclear Weapon -- That is non-negotiable!' [VERIFIED FACT -- no commitment] Trump declined to commit to a long-term ceasefire: 'I don't guarantee anything.' He has not said whether he accepted Iran's two-day proposal, which the Qatari PM reportedly presented in the meeting. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- market reaction] Brent crude settled down $5.75 (-5.85%) at $92.57/bbl on Nov 9 and extended losses after hours; WTI fell $3.98 (-4.38%) to $86.85 (Reuters-derived market reporting; AJ liveblog: 'Oil prices slump nearly 6 percent on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy'). [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Qatari side] The Qatari PM posted on X that he discussed 'the situation in the region and ways to progress the US-Iran talks' and was 'grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region.'
sections.what_verified: AP (T1 wire, via KXL mirror, published 21:52Z) + Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA flag; article + liveblog) carry the same on-record quotes from the briefing and the Truth Social post. Gulf Times and Shafaq News also carry it (no declared tier in the registry, not counted). The claim is Trump's own words, so the primary source is the President himself.
sections.what_disputed: Iran dismisses the remarks: SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei posted 'The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government... FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.' (AJ). President Pezeshkian said Khamenei called for an end to the 'neither war nor peace' situation and Iran is open to negotiations but 'will not surrender to force and bullying'; FM spokesman Baghaei said Tehran wants an end to hostilities on all fronts plus lifting of the blockade and sanctions before talks resume. Secretary of State Rubio said Nov 8 there had been little progress and he would not call the sides 'on the verge of a breakthrough'. Trump himself refused any long-term ceasefire guarantee and kept the blockade + Iron Gate in force; fighting continued through the weekend (tankers hit in/near Hormuz, Qeshm strikes Nov 8-9). AP notes these were Trump's 'most definitive comments about moving away from his threat to resume strikes' after the midterms — a posture statement, not a deal: no ceasefire, no agreement text, no Iranian acceptance.
sections.why_matters: Trump just declared the Iran war 'effectively over' — but the blockade stays, the carriers stay locked and loaded, and he won't guarantee a ceasefire. Oil crashed 6% on the words alone. So what exactly ended?
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- Trump declares Iran war 'effectively over' after Qatar PM meeting: 'we're just keeping it the status quo' — blockade + Task Force Iron Gate stay, no ceasefire guaranteed; Brent crude falls ~6%

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump just declared the Iran war 'effectively over' — but the blockade stays, the carriers stay locked and loaded, and he won't guarantee a ceasefire. Oil crashed 6% on the words alone. So what exactly ended? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the war actually over, or is 'effectively over' just a new name for a blockade that never lifts — and who pays while the status quo continues? Comment threads split between 'peace through strength, thank you Mr President' and 'Iraq-redux warmongering, fake news', with the blockade-vs-peace question at the centre.
